description: 'Eight Immortals'. A powerful and assertive clonal Dan Cong cultivar, developed from eight cuttings of a venerable Song Zhong mother tree. It is renowned for its intense, almost aggressive fragrance and a strong, impactful flavor profile that sets it apart from more delicate floral types.
parentage: Clonal selection from a Song Zhong mother tree.
plant_type: Vigorous arbor type with dark green, shiny leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in the high-altitude, rocky terroir of the Phoenix Mountains, which provides the mineral foundation for its strong character.

The liquor is a deep golden-amber."}
processing_suitability_details: The processing of Ba Xian requires a firm hand to manage its inherent power. The leaves are robust and can handle significant bruising to develop their strong aromatic compounds.
oxidation_details: Undergoes a medium-to-heavy oxidation (40-55%) to build a complex flavor base that can support its powerful aroma and assertive character.
roasting_details: Receives a medium charcoal roast. This helps to tame its natural intensity, integrate its flavors, and build a lasting, resonant finish without overpowering the core aroma.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. Ba Xian is a singular expression of a powerful, high-aroma Dan Cong oolong and is not used for other tea styles.

description: 'Purple Juan'. A unique and modern Yunnan cultivar developed from a natural purple-leaf mutation of the Da Ye (Assamica) varietal. Its most striking feature is its deep purple leaves, buds, and stems, a result of a very high concentration of anthocyanins. The finished tea has a distinct flavor profile, often with berry-like and slightly medicinal notes.
parentage: A clonal selection from a natural purple-leaf mutation of C. sinensis var. assamica.
plant_type: Upright, medium-sized bush with a striking purple coloration throughout the plant (Camellia sinensis var. assamica).
optimal_environment: Grown in the high-altitude tea regions of Yunnan, where strong sunlight is thought to enhance its purple pigmentation.

processing_suitability_details: Processing Zi Juan requires care to manage its higher-than-average astringency and bitterness. The processing method (green, black, or Pu'er) dramatically changes its final flavor profile.
oxidation_details: Oxidation levels can vary from none (green/Pu'er) to full (black tea). Full oxidation can help to mellow some of its natural astringency.
roasting_details: No roasting is typically applied. Like Pu'er, it is often sun-dried for green tea styles, or oven-dried for black tea styles.
style_versatility: Moderately versatile. It can be crafted into several different types of tea, but its unique and assertive flavor profile means it will always be a niche, specialty product rather than a mainstream tea.

description: 'Qimen Species'. This is not a single clone, but the local heirloom population of small-leaf tea bushes from Qimen county, Anhui. It is the one and only material used for making Keemun black tea. When processed into black tea, it produces a famously complex aroma with notes of wine, rose, pine, and dried fruit, earning it the title 'the Burgundy of tea'.
parentage: The native, local heirloom population of Qimen county.
plant_type: Small-leaf, genetically diverse bushes adapted to the local terroir (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in the mild, humid, and often foggy climate of Qimen county in southern Anhui, where the soil and environment are perfect for developing its complex aromatics.
tea_expressions: {"Black Tea": {"Keemun (Qimen Hongcha)": "Its only expression. A world-famous black tea known for its incredible aromatic complexity. Different grades exist, like Hao Ya (downy buds) and Mao Feng (pointed leaves)."}}

processing_suitability_details: The key to producing Keemun's unique aroma is a slow, carefully controlled withering and oxidation process. This allows the full range of aromatic compounds within the Qi Men Zhong leaves to develop.
oxidation_details: Undergoes full oxidation (100%). The oxidation process is meticulous and often takes longer than for other black teas, which is crucial for building its signature layered aroma.
roasting_details: A final, gentle drying bake is applied to stabilize the tea and halt oxidation. It is not roasted in a way that would impart a toasty flavor.
style_versatility: Completely specialized. The Qi Men Zhong population is only used to produce Keemun black tea. Its global fame is entirely dependent on this one style.
